analysis:
All three changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/...). They add no production code paths, endpoints, key handling, or trust-boundary changes, so no concrete security regression was found.

UnreclaimableLoadMemoryFixture.swift (lines 6-12, 66-67, 117-127) adds a ScriptedCounter and counts Super loads that reach the scripted loader, which always throws. It writes no secrets and loads no weights. The fixture uses temp directories, stub bridges, and an inert engine.

ProviderLifecycleTests.swift (head lines 220-242) adds a test that shutdownBeforeRegistration completes even when a slot is stuck unloading, because native retirement is unproven. It documents that process exit releases the memory. This relates to the availability concern in T-010/T-029 and to A-018. It checks that shutdown is not blocked forever (liveness) and does not weaken the drain semantics tested elsewhere. The production shutdown code is not in this batch, so I cannot confirm that it matches the test's claim. That is only a coverage limit, not a finding.

ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift (patch lines 189-229) adds a test that daemon state reports enabled_models_at_start and enabled_models_at_last_switch after a committed or refused switch, and that the saved config matches. It uses a mock coordinator and a temp root, and touches no TB-002 behavior beyond the mock. The base text for this file was not supplied, but the patch is self-contained.

The production code behind these tests (shutdownBeforeRegistration, the switchModels rollback, the daemon-state writer) was not supplied. Integration should verify that production behavior matches what the tests assert, notably that shutdown with retained unloading slots does not skip drain or acknowledgment steps required elsewhere.
